target_audience: Adult readers of international thrillers and military fiction
book_summary: A mysterious explosion sinks a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, blocking the world's most important energy chokepoint. As oil markets panic and naval forces converge, a cyber weapon of unknown origin turns the crisis into a war fought in silicon as much as steel. The novel follows an American destroyer officer, an Iranian naval captain, a downed pilot, a SEAL rescue team, and civilians on both shores as they try to survive choices made by leaders they will never meet.

chapters.name: Introduction
chapters.chapter_summary: The world wakes to news of a tanker explosion in the Strait of Hormuz. Commander Lin of the USS Truxtun and Captain Sharifi of the IRGCN watch the same crisis from opposite sides, each aware that the next hours could reshape history.
A tanker explodes in the Strait of Hormuz. Commander Sarah Lin and Captain Reza Sharifi converge on the disaster as minor skirmishes begin between fast-attack craft and coalition helicopters.
Oil prices spike; governments in Washington, London, and Dubai scramble. A cyberattack blacks out port infrastructure across the UAE, signaling a coordinated escalation.
Iran deploys mines, speedboat swarms, and coastal anti-ship missiles. The USS Truxtun protects minesweepers entering the strait under constant threat.
Amir, a disillusioned Iranian cyber-warfare technician, realizes the algorithm he helped write may have triggered the tanker incident. Cyber warfare cripples power grids and military networks.
Iran declares the strait closed to all traffic. Civilian tankers are trapped, and a boarding action puts the Orion Pride in danger.
Washington authorizes Operation Open Gate. Morales leads SEAD missions over the Iranian coast until his wingman is shot down.
Master Chief Miller's SEAL team races to rescue the downed pilot before Iranian security forces close in.

chapters.chapter_title: The Human Cost on the Home Front
chapters.chapter_summary: Zahra evacuates a hospital under coastal strikes in Bandar Abbas. Global fuel riots and supply shortages spread as the war touches civilians everywhere.

chapters.chapter_title: The Decisive Battle of the Chokepoint
chapters.chapter_summary: The coalition clears the strait in a devastating engagement. Lin and Sharifi match tactical wits across radar screens until the anti-ship missile sites fall.
A fragile ceasefire reopens the strait to limping traffic. Survivors face a changed world order.

chapters.name: Conclusion
chapters.chapter_summary: A fragile ceasefire reopens the Strait of Hormuz. Sarah Lin looks over a scarred ocean, Zahra begins to rebuild, and economists measure a changed world. A single tanker passes through at sunrise, escorted by wary warships—symbol of a tense, fragile normal.

all_characters.role: Executive Officer of the USS Truxtun
all_characters.psychological_depth: Calm under pressure; carries the weight of holding the line when the strait becomes a battlefield.
Aging pragmatist who understands the cost of escalation better than his superiors.
Her models predict catastrophe; she struggles to make leaders listen before markets crash.
Balances deterrence and diplomacy while hawks press for retaliation.
Flies SEAD missions knowing each sortie may be his last.
Leads a high-risk rescue because leaving a pilot behind is not an option.
Discovers his own code may have started the war and must decide what to do about it.
Works double shifts as her city collapses; her endurance becomes a quiet moral counterweight to the conflict.

all_characters.role: Civilian master of the Orion Pride
all_characters.psychological_depth: Trapped between navies, responsible for a panicking crew and dwindling supplies.
